Live-show feature

Eurovision duels — head-to-head trivia during the live show

A duel turns the dead air between performances into a battlefield. Challenge anyone in your room to a 3-question Eurovision trivia fight — winner steals their points or doubles their own. Two of the five end-of-night trophies (Duelist, Thief) are decided here.

What is a Eurovision duel?

A duel is a private 3-question Eurovision trivia round between exactly two players in the same room. Both players answer the same questions on a 12-second timer. The first question fires once the challenger accepts; everyone else in the room sees a discreet "duel in progress" chip but the questions stay private until the duel ends.

  • 3 questions. Pulled from the Eurovision trivia bank, weighted toward the room's decade preference.
  • 12 seconds per question. Score = 12 minus elapsed seconds, rounded down. Wrong or out of time = 0.
  • Winner takes the bigger answer total — plus a flat +12 win bonus.
  • Steal or Double. Winner picks one. Loser keeps their points if Double; loses up to winner_score if Steal.

When duels are available

Duels unlock from the Live Show phase onward. During the Preshow phase (lobby + predictions) all duel buttons are inactive — that's also when Quiz mode is open. Once the broadcast starts and the host advances to Live Show, Quiz locks and duels open. Both stay open through Results and Winners reveal.

Phase rule of thumb: Quiz is the warm-up, duels are the main event. You build score with predictions before the show, defend it with quiz before kick-off, then attack rivals with duels during commercial breaks.

Scoring math

The formula rewards speed and accuracy equally — a half-second hesitation costs you a point.

ScenarioPoints
Correct answer at 0–1 seconds11–12
Correct answer at 5 seconds7
Correct answer at 11 seconds1
Wrong / timeout0
Win bonus+12

The winner's total earned that duel is called winner_score. They then pick:

  • Steal — take winner_score from the loser's banked total. Capped at what the loser actually has (you cannot take them below zero).
  • Double — add another winner_score to yourself. Loser keeps their score.

Steal vs Double — when each one wins

⚔️ Steal

Zero-sum swing — your gain is matched by their loss. Use it when overtaking the leader matters more than the absolute gain (mid-show, leaderboard tight, you're second by 30 points).

✨ Double

Flat add — better when you're already ahead and don't want to fuel a revenge challenge. Strictly better when the loser has less than winner_score banked (no points to steal anyway).

How duels feed the trophies

Two of the five end-of-night trophies come straight from duel data:

  • Duelist — most duels won across the night.
  • Thief — most points taken via Steal.

See the full scoring page for how Duelist and Thief feed into the Champion total, and the rule book for sudden-death tiebreaks when two players tie a trophy category.
